clue.text: A light sweet

definitions.meaning: an old dark lantern with a thick convex lens that gives a concentrated beam
a large round striped peppermint boiled sweet sold in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: A double definition: a bull's-eye lantern is an old type of lamp, and a bullseye is a hard peppermint sweet popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are names: a lantern with a bulging lens and a striped round mint candy.

clue.text: Persian king upset over sex change

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits over, above, the next
in a down clue upset means the word is turned upside down, so read from the bottom up

parts.note: REX is Latin for king, the R in royal cyphers

indicators.note: a change to the letters of sex rearranges them into a new order

explanation.surface: A king of Persia is outraged by a sex-change operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns REX into XER, and 'change' rearranges SEX into XES, which goes under it. The famous ruler is defined only by 'Persian', with 'king' also feeding the wordplay in Rufus's loose style.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth-century BC ruler who invaded Greece was the most famous Persian monarch of all.

clue.text: Hear suit about writers' need for an alternative

indicators.note: about signals the letters of hear suit are moved round into another order

explanation.surface: Listening to a lawsuit about what authors require as an alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges HEARSUIT into the answer; 'Hear suit' reads like a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a word-finder book listing synonyms, which writers consult when they want a different word.

clue.text: Country put in a word of thanks for foreign capital

indicators.note: put in tells us the country is placed inside the word of thanks

parts.note: TA is informal British for thank you
Iran is a country in the Middle East

explanation.surface: Inserting a country name into a thank-you note for some overseas money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money; it is a capital city. TA is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Albania, so a capital abroad from a British setter's view.

clue.text: Made to smile by a thought?

explanation.surface: Someone smiles at a passing idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entertained enough to smile is the usual sense of the adjective.

clue.text: I heard a statement

indicators.note: heard means we want what is said aloud, not what is written

parts.note: the letter I is one of the five vowels, so it may be described as a vowel

explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is described as 'a vowel', and spoken that phrase sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An open declaration or admission is a kind of statement.

clue.text: They are linked with land measures

definitions.meaning: loops of metal joined together make up these
a surveyor's unit of length is 22 yards, used for fields and cricket pitches

explanation.walkthrough: A double definition: the old surveyor's length equals 22 yards, the length of a cricket pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a series of connected links and an old surveying unit of 22 yards.

clue.text: Journalist upset amid bad news for the country

indicators.note: amid means the reversed journalist sits in the middle of the other letters
bad signals that the letters of news are spoiled into a different order
in a down clue upset means the abbreviation is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is distressed by grim reports about a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' and 'upset' are both mood words in the surface; one shuffles, the other turns the editor upside down in this down entry, and 'amid' places that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian kingdom whose capital is Stockholm.

clue.text: Precipitate action for itinerant

indicators.note: action here means putting the letters of precipitate into motion and resettling them

explanation.surface: Rash conduct by a wandering traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' rearranges PRECIPITATE; all eleven letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone who travels from place to place for work.

clue.text: Star to cut back lighting unit

indicators.note: back tells us the word for to cut is read from right to left

parts.note: to lop is to cut off branches
the lux is the SI unit of illuminance

explanation.surface: Advice for reducing lamps to save energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut back' reads as one phrase meaning reduce, but it splits: 'back' reverses the lopping verb. Lux is the metric unit of illumination, one lumen per square metre.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the twin stars of Gemini, the brightest in the constellation.

clue.text: Takes a liberty?

parts.note: read literally: takes away someone's freedom, rather than behaving presumptuously

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase usually means being cheeky; here it means depriving someone of liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Making people into slaves literally removes their freedom.

clue.text: Not quick or not quick enough

definitions.meaning: quick in its old sense means alive, so not quick means dead, deceased
arriving after the expected time, tardy

explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' keeps its old meaning of living, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both deceased (quick meaning living) and behind time.

clue.text: Details put as specified in the agreement

indicators.note: as here implies the letters of details put are recast into a form that gives the answer

explanation.surface: Particulars written down as agreed in the contract.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is the slight word 'as'; DETAILS PUT rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Terms laid down as conditions of a contract are said to be required by it.

clue.text: Coordinates new colour schemes

indicators.note: new signals the letters of coordinates are made into a fresh word

explanation.surface: A designer matches fresh colour plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges COORDINATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Interior design work on paint and wallpaper is often called the decor or its plural noun.

clue.text: The prototype of an oil rig installation

indicators.note: installation suggests the letters are installed or set up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The first version of a drilling platform being set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installation' rearranges AN OIL RIG.
explanation.definitionFit: The first model from which copies are made is the master version.

clue.text: Fair verdict on an improved performance

definitions.text: Fair verdict on an improved performance

parts.words: Fair verdict on an improved performance
parts.note: a mild word of approval given when someone does reasonably well after a weaker effort

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a grudging compliment meaning fairly good.

clue.text: A dictum devoid of principles

parts.note: a moral is a lesson or maxim, a dictum

explanation.surface: A saying that has no principles behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironic surface: the principled 'moral' sits inside a word meaning without principles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without a sense of right and wrong lacks ethical standards.

clue.text: Look for a feature about double parking

indicators.note: double means the abbreviation is written twice

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
an ear is a feature of the face

explanation.surface: Searching for some attraction near a spot for double parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double parking' looks like a motoring offence; it means the parking abbreviation written twice, and 'about' puts the facial feature round that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to look, as in she appears tired.

clue.text: I'm in prison without money, that's the snag

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the prison word goes around the money

parts.note: a dime is a US ten-cent coin, a sum of money

explanation.surface: A broke prisoner explains what is holding them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' carries its old sense of outside, so the word for penned up wraps round the coin; 'in prison' looks like a container signal but is that synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle or hindrance is a snag in one's plans.

clue.text: Feel free, if inside tower

indicators.note: inside means the little word if goes into the middle of the other letters
free signals the letters of feel are released into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to make yourself at home in a tall building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feel free' sounds like a friendly invitation; 'free' shuffles the first word, and 'inside' puts the little conditional word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous iron tower in Paris is named after its engineer.

clue.text: A relation, not being heartless, makes a gift

parts.note: a relation is a telling, a narrative or story

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of not is removed, leaving the ends

explanation.surface: A relative without much heart still gives a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relation' looks like a family member; it is an account or story. 'heartless' leaves NT from NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude is often called a gift.

clue.text: First-class spinners

definitions.meaning: children's toys that spin on a point

explanation.walkthrough: A double definition; 'spinners' might suggest cricket bowlers, but these are toys.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the very best and whirling toys that spin on a point.

clue.text: You may read these at your convenience

definitions.text: You may read these at your convenience

parts.words: You may read these at your convenience
parts.note: convenience is British for a public toilet, so this is writing on lavatory walls

explanation.walkthrough: 'at your convenience' seems to mean whenever you like; in British English a public convenience is a public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrawled wall writing is classically found in public toilets, which Britons call conveniences.

clue.text: Turned to dole when sacked

indicators.note: turned signals the letters of to dole are turned around into another order

explanation.surface: A sacked worker had to go on the dole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' looks like dismissed from work; it means plundered. 'Turned' rearranges TO DOLE. The dole is British unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A city sacked by soldiers has been plundered.

clue.text: Tiny turned inlay that may have to be made up

annotationWithheld.why: Tiny turned inlay that may have to be made up (6): the only parse is WEE reversed in LAY, which needs inlay read as in lay; the one word inlay would be both container indicator and fodder
annotationWithheld.clue: Tiny turned inlay that may have to be made up

clue.text: Not just ugly

definitions.meaning: not beautiful, fair in the old sense meaning lovely

explanation.walkthrough: A double definition; 'just' looks like 'only', but it means fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both unjust and, in an old sense of fair, not good-looking.
